parole.significato: to hinder, to obstruct, to hamper, to be in the way (with dative)
parole.testo: Inherited from Proto-Slavic *vaditi. The primary meaning is likely a semantic loan from Polish wadzić (“to hinder, to obstruct”).

Inherited from Old Ruthenian доба (doba, “time, period”), from Proto-Slavic *doba (“time”). Considering that sense 1 (day, nychthemeron) was absent in Old Ruthenian, it is likely a semantic loan from Polish doba.

parole.significato: to covet, to crave, to thirst for, to hunger for, to ache
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian жадати, жедати (žadati, žedati), from Old East Slavic жадати (žadati), from Proto-Slavic *žędati. Sense 3 is probably a semantic loan from Polish żądać.
Ultimately from Proto-Slavic *mьžuriti via metathesis, likely borrowed from Polish mrużyć. Doublet of жму́рити (žmúryty).
Inherited from Middle Ukrainian мѣ́сто (místo), from Old East Slavic мѣ́сто (mě́sto), from Proto-Slavic *mě̀sto. Sense 1 is a semantic loan from Polish miasto.

parole.significato: to caress, to fondle, to cosset, to pet, to stroke
parole.testo: Inherited from Old Ruthenian пестити (pestiti), from Proto-Slavic *pěstiti, "e" instead of "і" in the root is unexpected, possibly borrowed from or influenced by Polish pieścić or Old Church Slavonic пѣстовати (pěstovati).
Inherited from Proto-Slavic *čajiti, later conflated with таї́ти (tajíty). Possibly borrowed from Polish czaić się. By surface analysis, чаїти (čajity) + -ся (-sja).
